sourceReadScope: Eight complete decisive source bodies were read, with unchanged complete prior reads reused for source profile, scenario, readiness observer, Host Windows launch and team model-readiness composition. New complete ModelProbeOwner, Main readiness-budget and OpenCode V1 member-provider bodies were read. The source-head and six CRLF joins bind the selected source; recorded dist/binary hashes are retained observations, not an independent rebuild.

codeBoundary.scenario: nativeEmulatedSourceScenario.ts original poll checks the 15,000 ms cutoff both before and after every awaited RPC, then sleeps 25 ms. The x64 stack is line 64: the post-await deadline assertion.
codeBoundary.openCodePreparation: OpenCode uses the original Main aggregate preparation before the independent readiness poll: captureRequestReadinessBudget(host.requestTimeoutMs), physical source/currentness capture and team.launch.start with that same budget. host.requestTimeoutMs is 15,000 ms. The later readiness poll has a separately started monotonic clock; it cannot renew the earlier readiness reference.
codeBoundary.exactRefusal: ModelProbeOwner.captureReadinessReference lines 198–205 reads the retained row, inspects its current target, checks admission/target/scope/not-retired and completed/ok/resourceHeld=false, then rejects Date.now() >= saved.expiresAt. Reaching phase probe-expiry therefore supports successful released model-probe completion but not a fresh reusable grant.
codeBoundary.consumer: inspectMemberModelReadiness reads the consumer and captures observedAt before calling readPreparedModelReference. Its later nested reference check can cross the same cutoff; the earlier observedAt is not a contradictory final observation.
codeBoundary.native: HostWindowsLaunch.RemotePending.prepare first sets phase=prepare and runs assertInput(true). An expired currentness callback causes current-false and failed() before the original native prepare request. 'dispatched' records remote allocation/staging admission; it does not establish native process dispatch.
codeBoundary.provider: The selected OpenCodeMemberProvider is V1 (1.18.35/1.19.4), not OpenCode V2 ModelProbe or the Codex driver. startServer uses captured custody and the original currentness/allocation guards; native.open failure seals/aborts, confirms stopped and preserves failure. No replacement grant or cached successful probe is accepted.

wallClockFacts.qualification: These are two retained Date.now samples in one refusal chain, not exclusive CPU/IO durations and not a globally atomic failure snapshot.

timing.clock: All per-job allocate/stage/prepare/resume/stop/drain/release timestamps below share the same Main epoch performance.now origin. The later 15,012.3773 ms readiness elapsed value uses its own later origin. Do not subtract those origins or infer wall-clock alignment.
timing.measuredScope: The observer measures original.handle(call) start through return/finally. Native prepare measurement ends before the additional capturedQueryableWitness wait. It does not measure total Host-side guard, serialization, IPC, scheduler, source/account/config inspection or event-loop time.
timing.gapsQualification: These are real uninstrumented intervals between separately observed Main handlers. They are not evidence that one named function or disk operation consumed the whole interval.
timing.jobPurposeQualification: Slot 0 is the reached finite version job. Source order and the retained completed-probe state support slot 1 as the preparation job; the stronger post-readiness probe-purpose/input assertions were never reached and are not promoted to PASS. Slot 2 is directly joined by its capability, original source reference and first-refusal jobSlot.
timing.missing: No common monotonic timing span identifies each existing Host currentness/reference/account/source facet and corresponding Main request send/receive interval. No per-facet duration or count covers the unobserved gaps.

cleanup.stdoutVersusFinal: The earlier slot-1 cleanup log had originalHandleAbsent=false before its final witness wait. The final receipt is true. Slot 2 remains originalHandleAbsent=false because no original root HANDLE exists; its complete confirmed-no-local-dispatch stop/drain/release proof is the applicable evidence.
cleanup.wrapperLimit: The wrapper's generic 'did not confirm cleanup' failure text is broader than the complete retained receipt/controller observations. Preserve source outcome INCOMPLETE and root exit 1; also preserve confirmed cleanup. Neither observation erases the other.
cleanup.globalLimit: The job's later compiler orphan cleanup is separate. No blanket claim that every OS process or future source execution was qualified is made.

precedingSuccessDetails.shared: Both complete receipts assert selected original A/B source identities, live and cold source rules, finite input/replay/management/standalone obligations and mandatory cleanup. All explicit realProviderExecuted, desktopQualified and releaseQualified flags remain false. Claude's original SDK-peer checkpoint restoration is true; Codex's is false and must not be promoted.

hostContracts.skipSummary: Two POSIX/Linux identity cases and the actual SDK POSIX-shebang test are Windows-skipped.

earlierJobScope.nativeNodeAndElectron: Each original gate records 25 named results with its expected negative-case exit statuses, complete bounded ownership checks and drained controller/root exit 0. The finite wrapper/peer subscenario is also PASS. These earlier bounded results are not an all-provider, GUI, release or whole-149/catalog-43/runtime-85 qualification.

armComparison.distinction: ARM failed Codex source-A at the pre-read line-62 cutoff while a catalog invocation remained before-await; its seven final original handles were absent. X64 completed Codex A/B and Claude A/B, then failed OpenCode V1 A at post-read line 64 with an explicit expired model reference and no native prepare on slot 2. Neither shared 'readiness timeout' wording nor physical slot/call count establishes a common cause.
armComparison.fourFreshCatalogChecks: The accepted no-reuse finding remains intact. This OpenCode failure supplies no basis for dropping, caching, reusing or parallelizing those separate Codex freshness boundaries.

boundedNextEvidence.repairStatus: No specific semantics-preserving latency repair is proved by the retained evidence. The expiry refusal itself correctly preserves the original cutoff and authority.
